sentences.text: This appeal is filed under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, the Act) read with Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short, the Code).
The present appellant - original opponent No.2
has assailed the judgment and order dated 27.09.2013 passed by the 3rd Additional Senior Civil Judge, Kheda, at Nadiad in LAR case No.86 of 2002.

entities.text: 3rd Additional Senior Civil Judge, Kheda, at Nadiad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The following order came to be passed by the learned reference Court:-
ORDER "(1) This reference is partly allowed.
(2) The market value of the acquired land is fixed at the rate of Rs.80,00/- per sq.m for irrigated land on 3.8.1999 (The dates of notification U/s 4 of the Act.).

1 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined (3) The opponents are hereby directed to pay jointly and severally the amount of additional compensation including amount granted u/s 23(1-A) and u/s 23(2) of the Act to the Claimants with 9% simple interest per annum for the first year from the date taking over possession and 15% simple interest per annum for the subsequent period till the date of payment with the proportionate cost.
(4) The claimants are entitled to get additional compensation at the rate of 12% of the market value U/s 23 (1-A) of the Act.
(5) The claimants are also entitled to get solatium U/s 23(2) of the Act at the rate of 30% on the additional compensation awarded.
(6) The claimants shall pay necessary Court fees as per the undertaking given by them subject to the decision given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
(7) The award be drown accordingly."
2. Heard learned Advocate Ms. Minoo A. Shah for the appellant, learned Advocate Mr. Varun G. Rai for respondent No.1- original claimant and learned AGP Mr. Aditya Davda for the respondent-State.
3. Brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1. An agricultural land bearing Survey /Block No.661/1 admeasuring about 1-09-84 square meter, situated in village Hariyala Taluka Matar, District Kheda was acquired by original opponent No.2 - present appellant for the purpose of tank loading, Parking L.P.G. NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined Plant.
The notification under Section 4 of the Act was published on 3.8.1999.
The declaration under Section 6 was published on 17.11.1999.
The Land Acquisition Officer by award dated 8.1.2001 awarded Rs.7.00/- per square meter for the acquired land.
The original claimant claimed compensation at Rs.150/- per square metre.
The said Award was challenged by the original claimants by filing a Reference Application under Section 18 of the Act.

The present appellant appeared in reference case and contented that the Land Acquisition Officer has awarded just and reasonable compensation after considering the fertility of the land and income of the crops.

After considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, more particularly the learned reference Court has relied upon the decision of this Court rendered in Special LAQ Officer & Another v. Jashubhai Vishabhai in First Appeal No.1364 of 2006 to 1373 of 2006 dated 21.12.2006, wherein the market value of the acquired land was assessed at Rs.54/- per square meter, fixed market value at Rs.80/- per square meter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award, the appellant is before this court.

Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited vs Manibhai Mangalbhai Baria on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15071056/
2 4.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the Appellant submitted that the learned reference Court has committed a grave error by simply NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined relying upon the decision rendered in Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra) and without assigning any reasons assessed the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.80/- per square meter.
It is submitted that the learned Court has mechanically awarded the compensation without considering the fact of the case of Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra).

In the aforesaid case, the purpose of acquisition was for National Highway No.8, whereas in the present case, the purpose of acquisition is for the parking of L.P.G. Plant and loading and unloading of tanks.
4.1. It is further submitted that the Land Acquisition Officer has after considering the evidence on record has assessed Rs.7/- per square meter for the acquired land.

The Land Acquisition Officer has also considered the earlier notification dated 16.12 1993 for acquiring the land for construction of National Highway No. 8 and also considered the purpose of acquisition of the land in question.

4.2. 
It is further submitted that the learned reference Court has committed an error by not appreciating the evidence which was considered by the learned Land Acquisition Officer.

In absence of similarity of the purpose of acquisition, the learned reference Court has committed a grave error in relying upon the market value which NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined has been assessed by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this court in the case of Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra).
4.3. It is therefore submitted that the aforesaid decision is not applicable to the facts of the present case.

Land Acquisition Officer had considered sale deeds of adjoining/
nearby Block of lands bearing block Nos.619, 654, 655 and 639/1 + 639/2 and after taking average sale value, development of village awarded Rs.7/- per square meters.

5. Per Contra, learned Advocate for the respondent No.1 - original claimant has vehemently submitted that the First Appeal is required rejection and no interference is needed in the order passed by the learned reference Court.
5.1.

It is further submitted that in the case of Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra), the acquisition proceedings were initiated pursuant to the notification under Section 4 of the Act which was published on 16.12.1993 for the same village Hariyala for the purpose of construction of National Highway No.8.
The Award was modified by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court by awarding compensation in all at the rate of Rs.54/- per square meter.
It is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined submitted that similarties in acquisition purposes is of no relevance.
What is important is the acquisition of land of same village.
Learned Reference Court has considered the most accepted method of assessing market value of the land in question.
6. I have considered the submissions and the papers available on record.
Undisputedly, the land in question was acquired by the appellant for the purpose of tank loading, Parking L.P.G. Plant.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.7/- per square meter.
The learned reference Court after considering the decision of Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra), fixed the market value of the acquired land at Rs.80/- per square metre.
Whereby additional compensation was awarded at the rate of Rs.73 per square metre (Rs.80/- per square meter - Rs.7/- per square meter = 73 per sqaure meter).

It is to be noted here that the purpose of acquisition in the present case is different than the purpose of acquisition in the case of Special LAQ Officer & Another Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited vs Manibhai Mangalbhai Baria on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15071056/
3 (supra).

entities.text: Special LAQ Officer & Another Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited vs Manibhai Mangalbhai Baria on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid case Section 4 notification was issued on 16.12.1993 and after considering the documentary evidence such as sale instances and another evidences, the reference Court awarded additional compensation to the claimant at the rate of Rs.49.50 paisa per square metre,
which was upheld by the Hon'ble Division Bench NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined of this Court.
Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra), fixed market value at Rs.80/- per square meter.

In the present case, the learned reference Court has awarded additional compensation by taking into account an award of a Court, fixing the market value of comparable lands, both in time and quality, which is one of the methods or modes of determining the market value.

The original claimant has relied upon the decision of Special LAQ Officer &
Another (supra) in determining the valuation.
Learned advocate for appellant could not point out anything from the Act, which precludes Court to consider purpose of acquisition in awarding compensation.
In my view purpose of acquisition is not the relevant factor for deciding market value.
When the lands of same village is acquired, the previous decision of Court in arriving at market value is one of the well accepted method.
6.1. In my view, reliance placed upon of the decision of Special LAQ Officer & Another (supra) is not a perversed finding.
In the present case, the learned reference Court has added 60% appreciation in the value for determing market value of land in question in the year 1999.
In the previous case of Special Land (supra), Section 4 notification was of year 1993.
As discussed above, similarity of purpose of acquisition of the land in 1993 with the land NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2107/2014 ORDER DATED: 04/10/2024 undefined in question in the 1999 has no relevance.
Thus, the learned Court has not committed any error in fixing the market value at the rate of Rs.80/- per square meter.

Thus, the judgment and order dated 27.9.2013 passed by 3rd Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Nadiad is hereby confirmed.
The appeal stands dismissed.
6.2. Record and proceedings to be sent back to the concerned reference Court forthwith.
No order as to costs.
